answer: The network binds each agent’s cryptographic credential to a physical‑world payment pulse, so a new identity must inherit the same vault timing ridge as its predecessor. When a node registers, it presents the latest pulse hash; the system checks the ridge of timestamps against the nadir of known Sybil clusters and merges matching entries into a single trust entity. An attacker must duplicate the exact payment source and reproduce the pulse ridge for every fake node, raising the cost to the price of multiple real transactions and continuous timing coordination.
